name: Dumbbell Side Bend
summary: A unilateral core exercise that isolates the obliques and quadratus lumborum through spinal lateral flexion.

setup: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart, holding a single dumbbell in one hand with your arm extended at your side.
Place your opposite hand behind your head or resting on your hip.
Brace your core and ensure your hips and shoulders are squared forward.
steps: Lower the dumbbell slowly down the outside of your thigh by flexing your spine directly to the weighted side.
Descend until you feel a moderate stretch along the opposite side of your torso, keeping your pelvis stationary.
Contract the obliques and quadratus lumborum on the unweighted side to pull your torso back to the vertical starting position.
Pause briefly at the top before beginning the next repetition, and complete all reps on one side before switching hands.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower the weight to the side; exhale as you contract to return upright.
cues: Move between two panes of glass.

common_faults.fault: Holding dumbbells in both hands simultaneously.
common_faults.correction: Hold only one weight at a time to prevent the opposing dumbbell from acting as a counterbalance.

common_faults.fault: Twisting or flexing forward at the spine.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a strict sideways bend in the frontal plane without rotating your torso or rounding your back.

common_faults.fault: Shifting or swaying the hips to the side.
common_faults.correction: Keep your pelvis anchored and stable, ensuring the movement originates entirely from the spine.

precautions: Avoid using excessively heavy loads that compromise spinal alignment or cause pinching sensations in the lower back.
